intro: Jewellery, keepsakes and the things that go in a toilet bag.
p.joya.consejo: The j sounds like an h: «HO-ya». The shop where they are sold is called «joyería».
p.anillo.consejo: The double l sounds like «y»: a-NI-yo. A wedding ring is called «alianza».
p.collar.consejo: The double l sounds «y»: ko-YAR. It is also the band a dog wears round its neck.
p.pendientes.consejo: It is almost always plural: «unos pendientes». A single piece is «un pendiente».
p.pulsera.consejo: It comes from «pulso» (pulse): the bracelet goes round the wrist, where you feel the pulse.
p.oro.consejo: To say what material something is made of, use «de»: «un anillo de oro».
p.plata.consejo: In many countries of Latin America «plata» also means «money».
p.recuerdo.consejo: It has two meanings: what you remember and the object you keep. It comes from «recordar».
p.perfume.consejo: It is masculine: «el perfume». The stress is on the syllable «fu»: per-FU-me.
p.peine.consejo: It has the diphthong «ei»: PEI-ne. The verb is «peinar» or «peinarse».
p.secador.consejo: It comes from «secar» (to dry). You say «secador de pelo» or just «secador».
p.tirita.consejo: It comes from «tira» (strip). In parts of Latin America people say «curita».
p.pintarse.consejo: With body parts you use the article: «me pinto los labios», not «mis labios».
p.bolsa de aseo.consejo: «Aseo» is personal hygiene. On a trip, all your bathroom things go in the «bolsa de aseo».
b1.texto:
Today we talk about jewellery, keepsakes and bathroom things.

- **Jewellery:** a **joya** can be an **anillo** (on a finger), a **collar** (round the neck), a **pulsera** (on the wrist) or **pendientes** (on the ears). The material takes **de**: **de oro**, **de plata**.
- **Llevar, ponerse, quitarse:** **llevar** is to have it on; **ponerse** is the action of putting it on; **quitarse** is the opposite.
- **Keepsakes:** a **recuerdo** is both what you remember and the object you keep: «es un recuerdo de mi abuela».
- **In the bathroom:** the **peine** and the **secador** are for your hair. The **perfume** and the **bolsa de aseo** travel with you.
- **Make-up:** **pintarse** los labios. With body parts you use the article: **me pinto los labios**, not «mis labios».
- **First aid:** a **tirita** is for a small cut.
b2.f0.texto: Have you put the toilet bag in the suitcase?
b2.f1.texto: I'm bringing the comb, the hairdryer and the perfume.
b2.f2.texto: I'm going to wear the silver necklace and my mother's earrings.
b2.f3.texto: Aren't you going to wear your grandmother's gold ring?
b2.f4.texto: That ring is a very important keepsake.
b2.f8.texto: Then put some plasters in the toilet bag.
b4.titulo: What it is made of and what you put on
b4.texto:
Two things are worth knowing:

- **The material** is said with **de**: un anillo **de oro**, un collar **de plata**, una puerta **de madera**.
- **With the body and clothes** you use the article, not the possessive, when the verb is reflexive: **me pinto los labios**, **se pone el collar**, **nos lavamos las manos**.

Three verbs help you talk about what you wear: **llevar** (to have it on), **ponerse** (to start wearing it) and **quitarse** (to stop wearing it).
b4.e0.texto: She puts on lipstick before the party.
b4.e1.texto: I take off the gold ring to wash the dishes.
b4.e2.texto: Your grandmother wears a silver bracelet on her wrist.
b5.f0.texto: In a drawer in the bedroom sleeps a box of dark wood.
b5.f1.texto: When it is opened, a soft smell of old perfume comes out.
b5.f2.texto: Inside shine a gold ring, a silver bracelet and two small earrings.
b5.f3.texto: Each piece keeps the memory of a loved one.
b5.f4.texto: The light from the window touches the gold and fills it with reflections.
b5.f5.texto: A girl of eight sits in front of the mirror.
b5.f6.texto: Very carefully she puts on the earrings and paints her lips.
b5.f7.texto: Her mother watches her from the door and smiles.
b5.f8.texto: The perfume fills the room with a sweet smell.
b5.f9.texto: When she gets up, the girl feels grown-up and happy.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! The bracelet goes round the wrist.
b6.o1.refuerzo: On the ears you wear earrings.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Round the neck you wear a necklace.
b6.pregunta: Where do you wear a bracelet?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Con» means «with». For the material you use «de».
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! Un anillo de oro: «de» says what it is made of.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «En» shows place. For the material you use «de».
b8.frase: Ella se pinta los labios antes de salir
b8.traduccion: She puts on lipstick before going out
b9.o0.refuerzo: The comb tidies the hair but does not dry it.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The plaster covers a small cut.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! The hairdryer blows hot air and dries the hair.
b9.pregunta: What do you use to dry your hair?
b11.o0.refuerzo: Exactly: with the body you use the article.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Se pinta» already shows they are her lips; «sus» is not needed.
b11.o2.refuerzo: They are her own lips: you say «los», not «unos».
b12.o0.refuerzo: A «recuerdo» is not today's purchase but something that makes you think of her.
b12.o1: algo que me hace pensar en ella
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! A keepsake holds the memory of a person.
b12.o2.refuerzo: A keepsake is kept, not lost. Think of memory.
p.metido.consejo: Past participle of «meter»; «has metido» means you have put something in.
p.llevar.consejo: «Llevar» means both carrying and wearing something on the body.
p.perderlo.consejo: With the pronoun attached: «perder» plus «lo» gives «perderlo».
p.déjalo.consejo: Informal command of «dejar»; the accent goes on the é of «déjalo».
p.daño.consejo: «Hacer daño» means to hurt; the ñ sounds like «ny».
p.mete.consejo: Informal command of «meter»: it means put in.
p.tiritas.consejo: «Tirita» is one small plaster; the plural adds «-s».
p.labios.consejo: «Labio» is one lip; «labios» is the plural.
p.quito.consejo: From «quitar»; the q sounds like k before i.
p.lavar.consejo: The v sounds like a b in Spanish: «lavar».
p.abrirla.consejo: «Abrir» plus «la» gives «abrirla»: the pronoun attaches to the infinitive.
p.pieza.consejo: «Pieza» is a piece or an item; the z sounds like th in Spain.
p.reflejos.consejo: «Reflejo» is one reflection; the j sounds like h.
p.ante.consejo: «Ante» is a formal word for «delante de»; it is used in formal writing.
